info.name: Sai Krishna Homes API
info.description:
All backend routes. 1) Start the backend (cd backend, npm run dev). 2) Run "Login" first: Postman keeps the session cookie for localhost automatically, so the admin requests work after it. 3) Run the folders top to bottom.

baseUrl defaults to http://localhost:8787. Set email/password collection variables to your admin login.

  "email": "",

  "message": "Requested visit",
  "visitAt": "2026-12-01T03:30:00.000Z"

item.name: 8. Projects (owner / co-owner)
item.description: Owners add new projects, fix a spelling (leads and visits move to the new name) and delete a project nobody uses. Panchawati Residency and Sai Krishna Residency are locked. Every change goes into the project history and the Activity log.

exec: pm.test("Both website projects are there and locked", () => {
pm.test("Has an id and history", () => { pm.expect(p.id).to.match(/^PRJ-/); pm.expect(p.history.length).to.eql(1); });

request.description: Names are compared ignoring case and extra spaces.

item.name: Add a lead on the new project
Delete while a lead uses it → 409

exec: pm.test("Says how many leads use it", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().leads).to.eql(1));

pm.test("Renamed, change recorded", () => { pm.expect(p.name).to.eql("Postman Valley Residency"); pm.expect(p.history[0].changes.name.from).to.eql("Postman Valey Residency"); pm.expect(p.history[0].moved.leads).to.eql(1); });

item.name: The lead now shows the new name

exec: const b = pm.response.json(); const all = Array.isArray(b) ? b : b.leads;
pm.test("Lead project renamed", () => pm.expect(all.find((l) => l.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("leadId")).project).to.eql("Postman Valley Residency"));

item.name: Activity log has the project changes
9. Recycle bin & hand over (owner / co-owner)
item.description: Delete never destroys a lead: it goes to the recycle bin (leads_trash) and the owner can restore it with all its calls and history. Only Fidelsya (superowner) can remove for good. Hand over gives every OPEN lead of one person to another (won/lost stay with who closed them). Everything is in the Activity log.

item.name: Delete it (goes to the recycle bin)

exec: pm.test("Lead is in the bin with who deleted it", () => { pm.expect(l).to.be.an("object"); pm.expect(l.deleted.by.email).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(l.deleted.at).to.be.a("string"); });

request.description: The owner can delete forever from the recycle bin, but only with confirm: "DELETE" (see folder 12).

exec: pm.test("Restored with a history line", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()[0].history[0].text).to.include("Restored from the recycle bin"));

item.name: Give the bin lead to the leaving person
Hand over all their open leads
Lead now with the new person

exec: pm.test("History says handed over", () => pm.expect(l.history[0].text).to.include("Handed over from Postman Leaving to Postman Taking"));

item.name: Hand over to the same person → 400
Clean up: delete the test lead
10. Management (CMO / GM)
item.description: Management = senior people such as the CMO and GM. They get every power the owner has (20 of 20 permissions ticked), but the owner holds the keys: only the owner (or Fidelsya) can create, edit, reset or deactivate them and untick any power. Management can manage sales / site visit executives only, never the owner or each other, and cannot hand out a power they do not have. Run top to bottom: it logs in as the owner, then the CMO, then the owner again.

item.name: CMO: may only create sales / site visit

exec: pm.test("Owner-level power not given to sales", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().permissions).to.eql(["leads.create"]));

request.description: Management cannot change the owner or each other.

item.name: Owner: take away the activity log from CMO
Activity log: what the CMO did

exec: pm.test("CMO created the sales exec", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().some((a) => a.type === "admin_created" && a.email === pm.collectionVariables.get("cmoEmail"))).to.be.true);

item.name: 11. Duplicate lead & deal value check
item.description: Duplicate: a mobile number that is already a lead (or in the recycle bin) is stopped with 409 and the list of who has it; sending allowDuplicate: true adds it anyway, marked on the lead (duplicateNote) and in the Activity log (lead_duplicate_added). Staff without "See all leads" only see who has the customer. Deal value: a won value that looks wrong gets 422 with the reasons; confirmValue: true saves it (valueCheck on the lead + deal_value_confirmed in the Activity log). A value outside ₹1 lakh – ₹50 crore can only be confirmed by the owner / Management / Fidelsya.

item.name: Is this number already a lead?

exec: pm.test("Found, with who has it", () => { const d = pm.response.json().duplicates; pm.expect(d.length).to.be.above(0); pm.expect(d[0].owner).to.be.a("string"); });

item.name: Clean up: delete both test leads
12. Delete forever (owner only)
item.description: Owner only (not Management, not staff): "Delete forever" from the recycle bin needs confirm: "DELETE". The leads are gone from the CRM for everyone; Fidelsya keeps them 120 days in a hidden archive (GET /api/leads/archive, restore, purge: Fidelsya only), then MongoDB removes them by itself. Recorded in the Activity log (leads_purged) with who, how many, the IDs and names.

exec: pm.test("Not in the bin", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().some((l) => l.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("foreverId"))).to.be.false);

item.name: Activity log: who, how many, IDs and names
13. Phone notifications (installed app)
item.description: Each browser that turns notifications on sends its push "subscription"; it is stored in push_subscriptions with whose it is. A website enquiry then sends "New website enquiry" to everyone who may see enquiries. Logout removes the device. The server needs VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY / VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY / VAPID_SUBJECT (publicKey is "" without them). Real delivery can only be tried from a browser (My account → Turn on notifications → Send a test).

item.name: Send a test with no device → 400 / 503

exec: pm.test("400 (no device) or 503 (no keys on server)", () => pm.expect([400, 503]).to.include(pm.response.code));
